title: Marda and the Moonpetal Seeds
markdown:
Nestled high in the misty mountains lived a young ogre named Marda. Not the sort of ogre in rough-and-tumble tales. A heart as gentle as a soft breeze, and a promise he held dear. Life in the mountains was full of simple happy things. Every day he helped his friends: the softest moss for cozy homes, stories that danced like firelight. Brum the marmot, who loved long naps and wise sleepy thoughts, often snoozed nearby, whiskers twitching. Luna Bright, the mountain goat whose hooves seemed to dance on steep slopes, would nuzzle Marda’s big green hand, her bleat a cheerful song.

Marda had made a solemn promise to his grandmother, when she was still with them: always leave the rare Moonpetal flowers untouched. They bloomed only once a year, petals delicate as tiny pieces of the moon, under the harvest moon.

Every day moved as smoothly as a mountain stream. Wake with the sun painting the peaks, big soft feet almost silent on the cave’s stone floor. Breakfast of plump dewy berries and warm honey cakes. Happy laughter off ancient rock walls. Brum rumbling a sleepy hello. Luna baaing a cheerful tune. A life as peaceful as a hidden meadow. Marda, truly, was content.

Until one day a gust of wind, not just a breeze, a truly mischievous swirling wind, tumbled into the mountains with a playful roar. It tugged at the moss Marda had gathered, ruffled Luna Bright’s fur, and then did something that made Marda’s heart sink like a stone into a deep well: it scattered the precious seeds of the Moonpetal flowers. Tiny shimmering seeds danced away, disappearing over tall rocky peaks. He knew, tummy sinking, that he had to get them back. His promise was in danger.

A tremble of worry. Empty patch of earth where the Moonpetals usually grew. Brow furrowed like a path after rain. How to keep the promise if the seeds were gone? He thought of his grandmother’s gentle smile, the one that always made him feel brave, and knew he had to try his very best. Courage, for a young ogre, is a very big thing. He set off into the shady ravines.

Along a rocky trail, eyes on the ground, a flash of green. On a sun-warmed rock, like a tiny king on a throne, a small elf, no bigger than Marda’s hand, ears like new leaves, eyes like morning dew. “Hullo there, tall one.” Tiny silver bells. “You seem to have lost something important.”

Marda explained, deep voice kept soft. “I promised my grandmother to leave the Moonpetals be. But the wind took their seeds, and now they are gone.”

The elf’s bright eyes grew wide. “Moonpetal seeds. Tricky little things. Finding lost treasures is my special job. Pipkin. Elf scout of these mountains.” He hopped down, graceful as a falling leaf. “Where did you last see them?”

Ogre and elf became the most unlikely, most helpful of friends. Pipkin, sharp eyes, able to fit into small places, a marvel. They followed the faint trail of shimmering dust. One tiny seed in the velvety cup of a sleepy sunflower. Another clinging to the soft fur of a passing cloud-sheep. One, quite remarkably, tumbled right into Brum the marmot’s mouth as he snored. Marda, very gently, woke the dozing marmot and took the seed from his snout. Pipkin, elfin charm, coaxed a stubborn seed from the ear of a grumpy mountain grumble-bug, who thought it was a new toy.

The seeds turned up in peculiar, perfectly sensible places. Marda, always a bit clumsy, learned to be even more careful, large hands moving with surprising gentleness. Pipkin learned that ogres, despite their size, could have the kindest hearts. They shared water from a cool spring, pure as fresh snow. Marda told Pipkin about the quiet joy of watching stars with his grandmother. Pipkin listened, bright eyes full of understanding.

As the sky blushed with twilight they spotted the last Moonpetal seed, on the very edge of a steep cliff where the wind usually howled. Air cooler. Wind a beautiful sad song. Pipkin, too small to reach, pointed with a tiny finger. Marda took a deep breath, stretched out his arm. Rough rock. Cry of a hawk. Sweet wild thyme. With great care he plucked the seed, cool against his skin, a tiny spark of moonlight in his palm. He had done it.

He walked back toward his cave, moon beginning its slow climb, seeds safe. He had not gathered a speech. He had gathered seeds, and a scout who fitted in small places, and a marmot who would go back to sleep. Luna Bright nuzzled his hand as if nothing unusual had happened, which, for a mountain, was almost true. The Moonpetals, when the harvest moon came, would find their patch of earth waiting. Marda put the seeds where the wind would have to ask more politely next time, which was how you knew a promise could chase a gust and still come home.
characters: Marda (young ogre who promised to leave Moonpetals untouched), Pipkin (an elf scout who finds lost treasures)
